biography_muhammad_muhammad_touray.text003: A Gambian educator, preacher and orator dedicated to teaching, guidance and community service. A graduate of Al-Azhar Al-Sharif, serving as teacher and Head of the English Department at Imam Malik Institute and as Imam and Khateeb of Abu al-Khair Mosque, Sukuta.
biography_muhammad_muhammad_touray.text009: From the Qur'anic learning circles of Gamibisara to the lecture halls of Al-Azhar in Cairo, the path of Muhammad Muhammad Touray has been shaped by a lifelong commitment to learning the religion and teaching it in the classroom, on the minbar, and through the airwaves.
biography_muhammad_muhammad_touray.text013: Born on 10 October 1973 in Koinya Kantora, The Gambia, Muhammad Muhammad Touray grew up in a family rooted in faith son of Muhammad Touray and Hajja Fatima Mama Omani. His early education began in the traditional majlis of the late Al-Haj Babou Fouti in Gamibisara, where he built his foundation in Qur'an and Islamic sciences.
biography_muhammad_muhammad_touray.text014: That early grounding sparked a desire to seek knowledge beyond his village, taking him to renowned centers of learning across West Africa and to Egypt.
biography_muhammad_muhammad_touray.text017: His pursuit of knowledge reflects the classic path of West African scholars moving between local scholars, specialized institutes, and university education.
biography_muhammad_muhammad_touray.text020: Began his studies in the council of the late Al-Haj Babou Fouti in the village of Gamibisara, learning Qur'an and foundational Islamic sciences.
biography_muhammad_muhammad_touray.text021: Dar al-Qur'an and Hadith Tuba, Mali
biography_muhammad_muhammad_touray.text022: Traveled to Tuba, Mali to study at Dar al-Qur'an and Hadith, deepening his knowledge in Qur'anic and Hadith sciences.
biography_muhammad_muhammad_touray.text023: Institute of Islamic Research Cairo, Egypt
biography_muhammad_muhammad_touray.text024: Joined the Islamic Research Institute (Ma'had al-Buhuth al-Islamiyya) in Cairo, affiliated with Al-Azhar, where he completed his secondary education with a very good grade.
biography_muhammad_muhammad_touray.text025: Al-Azhar University Faculty of Education, English Department
biography_muhammad_muhammad_touray.text026: Admitted to the prestigious Al-Azhar University in Cairo, Faculty of Education, English Department. He obtained his Licence (Bachelor's degree) with a good grade, combining Islamic education with strong English language training.
biography_muhammad_muhammad_touray.text029: His academic record shows consistent excellence: a primary certificate with excellent honors from Dar al-Qur'an and Hadith, a secondary certificate with very good honors from the Al-Azhar Islamic Research Institute, and a university licence from Al-Azhar University's Faculty of Education.
biography_muhammad_muhammad_touray.text030: This combination of traditional grounding and modern university training gave him the ability to teach in both Arabic and English, and to connect with diverse audiences.
biography_muhammad_muhammad_touray.text035: Teacher and member of the administrative board at Imam Malik Institute for Islamic Education.
biography_muhammad_muhammad_touray.text037: Leads the English Department at Imam Malik Institute, bridging Islamic knowledge and English education.
biography_muhammad_muhammad_touray.text040: Imam and Friday preacher at Abu al-Khair Mosque, Sukuta Serekunda, guiding the community through sermons and lessons.
biography_muhammad_muhammad_touray.text042: Regular preacher and advisor on Unique FM, extending religious guidance to a wider audience through media.
biography_muhammad_muhammad_touray.text046: Muhammad Muhammad Touray is known for his strong communication skills and ability to reach people across linguistic communities in The Gambia.
biography_muhammad_muhammad_touray.text047: His mother tongue is Soninke, alongside fluency in Mandinka and Wolof. In Arabic, he has very good command in both speaking and writing the language of his advanced studies. In English, the official language of The Gambia, he is also highly proficient in speaking and writing, a result of his specialization at Al-Azhar.
biography_muhammad_muhammad_touray.text048: This multilingual ability, combined with years of experience in teaching, administration, da'wah, and khutbah, has made him a trusted teacher, orator, and guide in his community.
biography_muhammad_muhammad_touray.text049: My Lord, increase me in knowledge and grant me understanding Muhammad Muhammad Touray
biography_muhammad_muhammad_touray.attr001: Original Arabic biography of Muhammad Muhammad Touray

biography_musa_muhammad_jibo.text001: Islamic University of Madinah • Student Affairs • Qur'an Center
biography_musa_muhammad_jibo.text003: A Gambian educator and administrator. Graduate of the Islamic University of Madinah in 2014, he serves as Deputy Director of Student Affairs at Imam Malik Islamic Institute and Head of the Supreme Committee at the Center for Qur'an Memorization and Islamic Studies.
biography_musa_muhammad_jibo.text008: From secondary studies at Ma'had al-Nour al-Islami in 2008 to graduating from the Islamic University of Madinah in 2014, Musa Muhammad Jibo has combined academic excellence with dedicated service to student development and Qur'an education in The Gambia.
biography_musa_muhammad_jibo.text011: From Basse to the City of the Prophet
biography_musa_muhammad_jibo.text013: Completed his secondary certificate at Ma'had al-Nour al-Islami in 2008, building a strong foundation in Islamic sciences and Arabic language.
biography_musa_muhammad_jibo.text014: Bachelor's Degree Islamic University of Madinah
biography_musa_muhammad_jibo.text015: Admitted to the Islamic University of Madinah al-Munawwarah, one of the world's most prestigious centers for Islamic learning. Graduated in 2014 with a Bachelor's degree, returning to The Gambia to serve in Islamic education.
biography_musa_muhammad_jibo.text018: During his time in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, he participated in six specialized training programs in 1435-1436 AH, reflecting a commitment to student development, intellectual awareness, and educational excellence.
biography_musa_muhammad_jibo.text020: Training program focused on Zakat education and community awareness, held in Saudi Arabia.
biography_musa_muhammad_jibo.text021: Qualification and Training of Distinguished Students 1435 AH
biography_musa_muhammad_jibo.text022: Program dedicated to nurturing and training outstanding students.
biography_musa_muhammad_jibo.text023: Human Chain Initiative to Reject Terrorism 1435 AH
biography_musa_muhammad_jibo.text024: Participation in a national initiative promoting peace and rejecting extremism.
biography_musa_muhammad_jibo.text026: Professional development project for graduating students, focusing on career readiness.
biography_musa_muhammad_jibo.text028: Course addressing intellectual challenges and their remedies, emphasizing critical thinking and authentic knowledge.
biography_musa_muhammad_jibo.text030: Specialized course in the sciences of the Prophetic Sunnah and its preservation.
biography_musa_muhammad_jibo.text034: At Imam Malik Islamic Institute, overseeing student welfare, discipline, and development programs.
biography_musa_muhammad_jibo.text036: At the Center for Tahfiz al-Qur'an al-Karim and Islamic Studies, leading strategic planning and academic oversight.
biography_musa_muhammad_jibo.text038: Trained in programs for distinguished students and graduate qualification, focused on building confident, capable students.
biography_musa_muhammad_jibo.text040: Engaged in initiatives promoting peace, rejecting terrorism, and addressing intellectual challenges facing youth.
biography_musa_muhammad_jibo.text044: His linguistic and personal skills support his educational leadership. Arabic at an excellent level the language of his university studies in Madinah. English at an intermediate level. Fluent in Soninke and Mandinka, connecting with diverse communities across The Gambia.
biography_musa_muhammad_jibo.text045: His training in student affairs, Sunnah studies, and intellectual awareness, combined with his administrative roles, positions him as an educator who cares for both academic knowledge and character building.
biography_musa_muhammad_jibo.text046: From Al-Madinah Al-Munawwarah to serving the Book of Allah in The Gambia Musa Muhammad Jibo

biography_omar_issa_dukureh.text001: Educator • Qur'an Memorization Specialist • Da'wah Supervisor
biography_omar_issa_dukureh.text003: An educator and specialist in Qur'an memorization and Islamic education. From traditional learning in Sierra Leone to leading educational roles at Imam Malik Institute in The Gambia since 2001, his life has been dedicated to teaching the Qur'an and serving da'wah.
biography_omar_issa_dukureh.text008: The journey of Omar Issa Dukureh bridges two West African nations and over three decades of service to the Qur'an. From memorizing the Book of Allah to supervising its memorization for generations of students, his path is one of dedication to education and da'wah.

Belonging to the Dukureh family, he received his early traditional education in Sierra Leone before his educational journey brought him to The Gambia, where he has since built his life of service.
biography_omar_issa_dukureh.text013: His formation combines traditional West African Islamic learning with formal Islamic education, centered on the Qur'an and its sciences.
biography_omar_issa_dukureh.text015: Learning, Memorizing, and Teaching the Qur'an
biography_omar_issa_dukureh.text016: His educational path reflects a lifelong relationship with the Holy Qur'an — as a student, memorizer, and later as a teacher and supervisor.
biography_omar_issa_dukureh.text019: Received his traditional Islamic education in Sierra Leone, building a foundation in Qur'an and basic Islamic sciences.
biography_omar_issa_dukureh.text023: Completed his primary and preparatory (intermediate) studies at Dar al-Qur'an and Hadith, focusing on Qur'an memorization and Hadith sciences.
biography_omar_issa_dukureh.text025: In 1984, he joined the Qur'an memorization department. He devoted himself to memorizing the Holy Qur'an, completing his memorization and receiving recognition for his efforts.
biography_omar_issa_dukureh.text027: Completed the memorization of the entire Qur'an in 1988, marking a major milestone that would define his future service in Qur'an education.
biography_omar_issa_dukureh.text030: Obtained his intermediate and secondary qualifications in The Gambia between 1992 and 1996, followed by higher studies. In 2001, he completed advanced studies in Shari'ah and Islamic education, with focus on Qur'an sciences and teaching methodology.

biography_omar_issa_dukureh.text051: First Director and later Deputy Director of Imam Malik Institute, shaping its growth since 2001.
biography_omar_issa_dukureh.text053: Supervisor of Qur'an memorization, guiding students in Hifz and Tajweed.

school_history_index.text007: The Official History of Imam Malik Islamic Institute
school_history_index.text008: The history of the institute begins with the founding of Samboudoukati Association in 1960. Its first headquarters was located in Banjul, in the house of Alhaji Musa Njai (may Allah have mercy on him) at 16 Lemon Street. When the place became too small, the association moved to the house of Alhaji Saibo Tankara on Lancaster Street.
school_history_index.text009: Education began in the traditional kuttab (Qur’anic school) style, with students attending morning and evening sessions.
school_history_index.text010: The teachers during this early period were:
school_history_index.text011: Sheikhba Sise (may Allah have mercy on him), the son‑in‑law of Alhaji Baba Kamara.
school_history_index.text012: Alhaji Baba Kamara (may Allah have mercy on him).
school_history_index.text013: Jindi Simiga Jani (may Allah have mercy on him).
school_history_index.text014: In 1996, the institute shifted from the traditional kuttab system to a formal academic system. The teachers at that time were:
school_history_index.text016: Ousman Muhammad Samba Drammeh – Deputy Director
school_history_index.text019: The primary stage (Grades 1–3) was opened in Banjul and continued until the year 2000. At that time, the institute was known as “Samboudoukati Islamic School”.
school_history_index.text020: In 2001, the association opened a new school in Kanifing, starting with Grade 5. Its name was:
school_history_index.text021: “The Islamic School for Qur’an Memorization and the Study of Islamic and Modern Sciences Samboudoukati Association Kanifing”.
school_history_index.text025: Later, the school in Banjul along with its students and teachers moved to Kanifing, led by the Deputy Director Ustaz Ousman Muhammad Samba Drammeh, after Director Malamin Jagna traveled to the United States. Drammeh then assumed full responsibility for managing the school.
school_history_index.text026: By 2002, the school had reached Grade 6. In 2003, the junior secondary level was opened. The first graduating class completed their studies in 2008/2009, consisting of eight male students.
school_history_index.text027: The institute witnessed significant growth with the arrival of two teachers in October 2004:
school_history_index.text028: Ustaz Muhammad Kaba Musa (may Allah have mercy on him)
school_history_index.text033: In 2005, the name of the institute was officially changed to:
school_history_index.text035: based on a suggestion from Dr. Fodi Baba Jagna while he was a student at the Islamic University in Madinah.

school_rolls.text008:
Student Statistics, Programs, Regulations,
            Admission and Future Development
school_rolls.text011:
Current statistics of students and graduates
                across the different departments of the
                Imam Malik Islamic Institute.
school_rolls.text025:
In addition to Arabic, English, Qur'an memorization
                and regular courses, the institute provides several
                community-focused programs.
school_rolls.text027:
A specialized program supporting Khateebs
                    serving in 21 mosques across Serrekunda
                    and its surrounding areas.
school_rolls.text029:
During the holy month of Ramadan, the institute
                    provides Qur'an interpretation sessions in the
                    Soninke language to make Islamic knowledge more
                    accessible to the local community.
school_rolls.text031:
The institute organizes annual visits to Arabic
                    and Islamic schools to strengthen educational
                    cooperation, exchange knowledge and build
                    relationships between institutions.
school_rolls.text034:
All students are expected to follow the institute's
                regulations and maintain an Islamic, respectful and
                disciplined learning environment.
school_rolls.text035:
Students must observe Islamic values and
                    practices in all their dealings, both inside
                    and outside the institute.
school_rolls.text036:
Fighting, stealing, unauthorized selling,
                    smoking, wearing garments below the ankles
                    and other actions contrary to Islamic teachings
                    are prohibited.
school_rolls.text037:
All institute teachers must be respected
                    without discrimination.
school_rolls.text038:
Bringing smartphones and similar electronic
                    devices to the institute is prohibited.
school_rolls.text039:
Students must arrive early wearing the official
                    institute uniform and must maintain its cleanliness.
school_rolls.text040:
Students are expected to take their studies
                    seriously and complete their homework.
school_rolls.text041:
Any form of inappropriate or unauthorized
                    relationship is strictly prohibited.
school_rolls.text042:
Students are not permitted to walk around the
                    institute grounds during class or prayer times.
school_rolls.text043:
Female students are expected to maintain
                    appropriate Islamic dress and modesty within
                    the institute.
school_rolls.text046:
Registration for any level of study is completed
                by visiting the institute and attending an interview
                to determine the student's appropriate level.
school_rolls.text048:
Students applying for lower levels,
                        including kindergarten, must attend
                        with their parent or guardian.
school_rolls.text049:
The applicant receives a registration form
                        containing student information and contact details.
school_rolls.text050:
The registration fee must be paid.
                        The fee is non-refundable.
school_rolls.text051:
The student's level is determined through
                        a personal interview.
school_rolls.text052:
The student's parent or guardian signs an
                        agreement confirming commitment to the
                        institute's rules and regulations.
school_rolls.text054: The student must be at least five years old.
school_rolls.text055:
The student must demonstrate good character
                        and conduct.
school_rolls.text056:
Students who previously attended another
                        institute must provide their academic record.
school_rolls.text057:
The student must agree to follow all institute
                        rules and regulations.
school_rolls.text059: A copy of the student's birth certificate.
school_rolls.text062:
Students can apply for admission at the
                    appropriate educational level according to
                    the institute's admission requirements.
school_rolls.text063:
Each student will participate in a personal
                    interview to determine the most suitable
                    academic level.
school_rolls.text066:
The institute aims to continuously improve its
                educational and administrative services while
                making information more accessible to students,
                parents and staff.
school_rolls.text068:
A sophisticated Artificial Intelligence system will
                be added to the website in the future. The system
                will be capable of answering questions about the
                institute and providing useful information to
                students, parents and staff, improving communication
                and making access to information easier.
school_rolls.text070:
Stay connected with the institute through its
                social media platforms.
